justification: Core DB connection handling change affecting all PostGIS queries. Not Critical because read-only queries, no schema changes, defense-in-depth pattern.

pre_impl.existing_data: spatial_overlays, dcp_setback_controls, housing_sepp_standards, tax_thresholds — all read-only
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: autocommit=True on read-only connection is safe — no multi-statement transactions needed
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applies to all existing DB calls immediately — connection pattern change, not data change

functions.name: fetch_dcp_setbacks
functions.output: dict with setback rows or None
functions.if_none: returns None — caller shows 'DCP not available'

functions.name: fetch_heritage_postgis
functions.output: dict with hca list, items list, has_heritage bool, raw list
functions.if_none: returns empty dict — caller shows no heritage from PostGIS

functions.name: fetch_lep_clauses
functions.output: list of clause dicts with number, heading, summary, source
functions.if_none: returns [] — caller skips LEP clause section in PDF

values.if_missing: reverts to psycopg2 default (autocommit=False) — cascading failure on error

queries.purpose: fetch DCP setback controls for an LGA
queries.if_zero: returns None — DCP section omitted from report
queries.if_wrong: wrong LGA's controls shown — mitigated by detect_former_council slug validation

break_it.scenario: autocommit=True with a connection that has an active transaction from caller code
break_it.what_happens: psycopg2 raises ProgrammingError: can't change autocommit state within a transaction
break_it.how: conveyancing.py creates fresh connections — no pre-existing transaction possible

break_it.scenario: conn.rollback() itself fails (e.g., connection already closed)
break_it.what_happens: rollback exception caught by bare except, function still returns safe default
break_it.how: conveyancing_db.py — every rollback is wrapped in try/except Exception: pass
break_it.repro: Mock conn.rollback to raise, verify function still returns empty/None

break_it.scenario: First query fails, rollback succeeds, second query returns stale/cached cursor data
break_it.what_happens: Would return wrong data from previous cursor state
break_it.how: Each function creates its own cursor via conn.cursor() — no shared cursor state

break_it.scenario: DCP setback query returns rows for wrong LGA due to slug mismatch
break_it.what_happens: User sees another council's setback controls — wrong regulatory data displayed
break_it.how: conveyancing_db.py:161 — WHERE lga = %s parameterised; slug comes from detect_former_council which maps known addresses to known slugs
break_it.repro: Call fetch_dcp_setbacks with invalid slug → returns None (no rows match)

post_merge.manual_verify: No — connection behavior change is tested by 6 new unit tests
